newsitem.title: CYPRUS: U.N. envoy to quit Cyprus meditation post.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy to quit Cyprus meditation post.

text.p: Former South Korean Foreign Minister Han Sung-joo said on Monday he would not seek an extension of his appointment as U.N. special representative to the divided island of Cyprus after a year at the post.

Han, whose term expires on April 30, said it would be in the best interests of the parties concerned to have an envoy who can devote more time to the issue, given the quickening pace of U.N. diplomacy to resolve the problem.

"In addition to the long distance between Cyprus and Seoul, my other responsibilities and commitments make it difficult for me to devote the amount of time necessary to the Cyprus problem during this period of intensified activity," Han told Greek and Turkish Cypriot journalists at a news conference in the divided Cyprus capital of Nicosia.
"The situation is not the same as a year ago when several visits a time would have been adequate," he added.

Cyprus, divided since Turkey invaded its north in 1974 in the response to a brief coup in Nicosia engineered by the Athens junta, has been the object of various mediation attempts at reunification. They have all failed.
The U.N. is now working on bringing the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities together before the end of June for the resumption of direct talks.
Earlier on Monday Han, who arrived in Cyprus on Saturday, had talks with President Glafcos Clerides, head of the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
If the U.N. is successful, it will stage the first meeting between the two leaders in almost three years.
"In a sense the results or the assumed success of our activities so far has made a different type of envoy necessary," Han said, dismissing suggestions he was abandoning a lost cause.

The United Nations has refused to divulge the specifics of the proximity talks, but Han said he was leaving the island with more optimism of a meeting with the two leaders than he was during his last visit in February.
The latest burst of diplomatic activity has been spurred by Cypriot hopes of joining the European Union. Membership talks would be greatly eased if the division of the island were ended.
